subject: ClearHarbor: approval request — data residency carveout + pilot discount
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Vance <michael.vance@clearharbor.com>, Susan Foley <susan.foley@clearharbor.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: exec signoff for residency carveout + pilot pricing (ClearHarbor)

Avery — looping you in for quick exec clearance. ClearHarbor wants to run a six-week private pilot in a VPC in us-west-2 but with the following non-standard asks: 1) data residency guarantee that all customer content remains in their dedicated VPC (they want an auditable proof of egress controls), 2) restricted audit window: their external auditors will need on-site access for a 3-day audit (they're requesting elevated audit rights), and 3) temporary exception to our standard SLA around cross-region failover during the pilot (they want no automatic cross-region replication).

Attached: SOW v3 and their security questionnaire. Legal has flagged the audit language as broad; engineering flagged the cross-region hold as a potential risk to our HA posture. The commercial ask: they want a pilot discount of 15% off list for the six-week pilot, plus a one-time $20k implementation credit.

Can you advise if we can approve the residency carveout with limited audit scope, and whether we have flexibility on the discount? I’ve summarized the tradeoffs below and recommended next steps.

Quick summary:
- Risk: audit scope + no cross-region replication reduces our ability to failover (Aditya, can you weigh in)
- Legal: audit language needs to be scoped and timeboxed (Markus will propose redlines)
- Commercial: pilot discount is above playbook for this segment (Laura, decision for final discount)

Next step requested: exec decision by EOD tomorrow to keep the momentum.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0197

Attachments: ClearHarbor_SOW_draft_v3.pdf, security_q_1206.xlsx

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exec signoff for residency carveout + pilot pricing (ClearHarbor)

Thanks for the concise summary, Marissa. I agree we should move quickly but carefully. High level: I’m supportive of allowing a controlled residency carveout for a pilot if we can get the following in writing: 1) audit scope strictly limited to production systems in the VPC and limited to specific data classes, 2) audit duration capped at 3 consecutive days with advance notice and on-site escort requirements, 3) a written acknowledgement that cross-region failover may be limited during the pilot and that ClearHarbor accepts the associated availability risk.

Markus / Aditya — please provide the minimum legal redlines and the minimum engineering guardrails we need to accept this safely. Laura — please advise on commercial flexibility. If we can get redlines by EOD I’ll sign off on the carveout and the principle of a pilot credit, subject to final discount approval.

Avery Johnson
VP, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: exec signoff for residency carveout + pilot pricing (ClearHarbor)

Avery / team — attached are tracked redlines (redlines_ClearHarbor_terms_0903.docx). High-level legal position: we can agree to a pilot-scope audit with the following constraints: 1) audit limited to systems processing ClearHarbor data in the specified VPC and scoped to listed control families (access logs, encryption-at-rest, network egress controls); 2) auditors must execute our standard NDA and provide proof of professional credentials; 3) audit duration limited to up to 3 business days with 14 days’ notice; 4) no right to copy or remove production datasets — read-only review under escort; 5) we need indemnity carveouts for any GDPR-adjacent claims stemming from auditors’ actions.

Engineering notes (Aditya): we can disable automatic cross-region replication for the pilot window but require a documented rollback plan and an SLA carveout noting acceptance of higher outage risk. Also we need a strong runbook that ClearHarbor signs off on for maintenance windows and emergency failback.

If we accept these redlines, legal can sign off on the residency carveout. I recommend we offer a limited commercial concession (discount) to secure the pilot but cap it.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: redlines_ClearHarbor_terms_0903.docx

Subject: Re: Request: exec signoff for residency carveout + pilot pricing (ClearHarbor)

Marissa / Avery — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed Markus's redlines and that's reasonable. Two asks before we sign: 1) pilot discount to 15% (we can commit to the six-week pilot and provide a success criteria doc), and 2) confirmation that the implementation credit is applied to integration work (we need it for SSO + custom VPC routing). If you can confirm the discount and credit, we’ll sign the SOW and schedule the audit week.

We understand the rollback requirements and will sign the runbook and NDA for auditors.

—Michael

Team — I spoke with finance. Given the strategic nature of ClearHarbor (potential enterprise anchor) and their willingness to commit to success criteria and an enforced runbook, I’m comfortable authorizing a pilot concession up to 12% and approving a one-time $12k implementation credit. Rationale: preserves margin playbook while keeping the deal moving.

If ClearHarbor absolutely needs 15% we can stretch but we need at least one of the following as compensation: (a) a firm 12-month paid commitment if pilot is successful, or (b) an increased list price post-pilot tying to usage thresholds. Marissa — can you close on one of those?

Laura Bennett
